mc001.questionText: Which of the following are mandatory when working at heights above 2 metres?
mc001.explanation: Working at heights requires fall protection (harness + lanyard), head protection and foot protection as minimum. Hi-vis and hearing protection depend on the specific environment.

mc002.questionText: Which of the following are classified as hazardous substances under REACH regulation?
mc002.explanation: Asbestos, benzene, and silica dust are all classified as hazardous substances with strict exposure limits. Drinking water and compressed air are not classified as hazardous under REACH.

mc003.questionText: Which of the following are valid methods to prevent fire in a workplace?
mc003.explanation: Fire prevention involves removing ignition sources, proper storage of flammables, and adequate ventilation. Water should not be used on chemical spills (may spread or react). Extinguishers must be accessible, not locked away.

options.a: Removing ignition sources near flammable materials
options.b: Storing flammable liquids in approved safety cabinets
options.c: Increasing ventilation to dilute flammable vapours
options.d: Using water to clean up all chemical spills
options.e: Keeping fire extinguishers locked away to prevent misuse

tf001.questionText: Indicate whether each of the following statements about hazardous substances is true or false:
tf001.explanation: SDS must be available per REACH regulation. Original containers prevent confusion. Chemical waste must follow specific disposal routes. Both liquids and gases can require ventilation.

statements.s1: An SDS (Safety Data Sheet) must always be available on site
statements.s2: Hazardous substances must be stored in their original containers
statements.s3: You can dispose of chemical waste in regular garbage
statements.s4: Ventilation is only required for liquids, not gases

tf002.questionText: Indicate whether each of the following statements about PPE is true or false:
tf002.explanation: PPE is the last resort in the hierarchy of control, not the first. Employers must provide PPE free of charge. Damaged PPE must be replaced. CE marking confirms compliance with EU safety standards.

statements.s1: PPE is the first line of defence in the hierarchy of control
statements.s2: The employer is responsible for providing PPE free of charge
statements.s3: Damaged PPE must be replaced immediately
statements.s4: PPE with a CE mark meets minimum European safety requirements

tf003.questionText: Indicate whether each of the following statements about working in confined spaces is true or false:
tf003.explanation: Confined space entry always requires a permit-to-work. Atmospheric testing is mandatory regardless of visible hazards (oxygen deficiency is invisible). A standby person and rescue equipment are always required.

statements.s1: A permit-to-work is always required before entering a confined space
statements.s2: Atmospheric testing is only needed if there is a visible hazard
statements.s3: A standby person must be present outside the confined space
statements.s4: Rescue equipment must be available before entry

ord001.questionText: Place the steps of the hierarchy of control (elimination to last resort) in the correct order, starting from the most preferred:
ord001.explanation: The hierarchy of control runs from Elimination → Substitution → Engineering → Administrative → PPE. PPE is always the last resort because it relies on correct use by the individual.

ord002.questionText: Place the steps for responding to a chemical spill in the correct order:
ord002.explanation: In a chemical spill: first evacuate and warn others, then identify the substance via SDS, then clean up with correct PPE and materials, and finally report the incident.

items.i1: Notify supervisor and complete incident report
items.i2: Evacuate the immediate area and warn others
items.i3: Clean up using appropriate absorbent materials and PPE
items.i4: Identify the substance using the SDS

ord003.questionText: Place the steps for using a fire extinguisher (PASS technique) in the correct order:
ord003.explanation: The PASS technique: Pull the pin → Aim at the base → Squeeze the handle → Sweep side to side. Always aim at the base of the fire, not the flames.

items.i1: Squeeze the handle to discharge the agent
items.i3: Sweep from side to side at the base of the fire
items.i4: Aim the nozzle at the base of the fire

mat001.questionText: Match each type of fire extinguisher to the class of fire it is designed for:
mat001.explanation: Water: class A solids only. Foam: class B liquids (and A). CO₂: electrical (class C) — displaces oxygen without leaving residue. Dry powder: versatile (A, B, C) but leaves residue.

rightItems.r4: Class A, B and C fires (multipurpose)

mat002.questionText: Match each safety sign colour to its meaning:
mat002.explanation: ISO 7010 colour coding: Red = prohibition/fire, Yellow = warning, Blue = mandatory, Green = safe condition/emergency. These are standardised across the EU.

mat003.questionText: Match each type of PPE to the hazard it primarily protects against:
mat003.explanation: Each PPE type is matched to its primary hazard. Ear defenders protect against noise. FFP3 respirators protect against fine particles. Goggles protect eyes. Anti-vibration gloves reduce HAVS risk from power tools.

rightItems.r2: Inhalation of fine dust and aerosols
rightItems.r3: Chemical splash or flying particles to eyes
